# upsnap_permission (Resource)

What an UpSnap user may do (`permissions` collection). Each user has at most one permission record. Requires superuser credentials.

UpSnap adds a device to the `read`, `update`, `delete` and `power` sets of its creator when a user creates a device, or when `upsnap_device.created_by` is set, and removes deleted devices from every set. Both show up as drift here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "upsnap_user" "alice" {
  username = "alice"
  password = var.alice_password
}

resource "upsnap_device" "workstation" {
  name = "Workstation"
  ip   = "192.168.1.30"
  mac  = "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:30"
}

resource "upsnap_permission" "alice" {
  user_id = upsnap_user.alice.id
  read    = [upsnap_device.workstation.id]
  power   = [upsnap_device.workstation.id]
}

variable "alice_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `user_id` (String) ID of the `upsnap_user` the permissions apply to.

### Optional

- `create` (Boolean) Allow the user to create devices and groups and to scan the network.
- `delete` (Set of String) IDs of devices the user can delete.
- `power` (Set of String) IDs of devices the user can wake, sleep, reboot and shut down.
- `read` (Set of String) IDs of devices the user can see.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `update` (Set of String) IDs of devices the user can edit.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Record ID.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = upsnap_permission.alice
  identity = {
    id = "nmj3ko20gzkg8n3"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Permission record ID.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = upsnap_permission.alice
  id = "username:alice"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By record ID
terraform import upsnap_permission.alice nmj3ko20gzkg8n3

# By user, since every user has at most one permission record
terraform import upsnap_permission.alice user:27do0wbcuyfmbmx
terraform import upsnap_permission.alice username:alice
```
